title: The Escrow Analysis and the Monthly Escrow Deposit It Sets on Home Mortgage Loans
content:
At intervals of the program's stated months between analyses, Piedmont Crescent Bank runs an escrow analysis on a Home Mortgage Loans note and resets the monthly escrow deposit on it.

**The projection.** The analysis projects the next 12 months. The projection is taken from the latest tax and insurance bills, by kind of bill, and yields both the escrow disbursements expected over those 12 months and the lowest escrow balance reached at any point within them.

**The deposit.** The monthly escrow deposit is set to the projected disbursements divided by 12, plus the amount needed to keep the lowest projected balance at the program's cushion, expressed in months of disbursements.

**A shortage.** A projected shortage is collected over the program's stated number of added installments.

**A surplus.** A projected surplus at or above the program's surplus refund threshold is refunded to the borrower after the analysis. A surplus below that threshold is credited to the next year's payments instead. A surplus is refunded only when the loan is current.

## Worked figures on hypothetical inputs

Take a loan on a program whose cushion is 2 months of disbursements and whose shortage is collected over 12 added installments.

The analysis projects disbursements of $6000.00 over the next 12 months. Divided by 12, that is $500.00 a month. A cushion of 2 months of disbursements on that projection is $1000.00. The lowest projected balance over the window comes to $400.00, so $600.00 is needed to bring it to the cushion. Collected over 12 added installments, that adds $50.00 a month. The monthly escrow deposit is therefore set to $550.00.

Now take the same loan a year later, where the analysis instead projects a surplus of $62.00 on a program whose surplus refund threshold is $50.00. The surplus is at or above the threshold, so it is refunded to the borrower after the analysis, provided the loan is current. Had the projected surplus been $38.00, it would have been credited to the next year's payments.
